title_orig: Περὶ τῆς ὀρθῆς καὶ ἀληθοῦς τῶν Χριστιανῶν πίστεως ὁμιλία (Confessio fidei posterior; De Christianorum recta et vera fide homilia ad sapientes Agarenos, hortatu magni Sultani et ipso praesente dicta)
title_es: Confesión de fe posterior (homilía sobre la fe verdadera de los cristianos, dirigida a los sabios agarenos por exhortación del gran sultán)
title_en: Confession of Faith (posterior): homily on the true Christian faith addressed to the wise Agarenes at the sultan's request
date: c. 1457-1458 (usual dating; not verified in this session)
language: Greek, with Latin printed beside it in Migne
edition_original: Migne PG 160, cols. 333A-352A (index: 'Confessio fidei II'). Greek OCR in the archive.org scan is badly garbled; the Latin is legible.
digital_url: https://archive.org/download/bim_early-english-books-1641-1700_patrologiae-cursus-completus-_1866_160/bim_early-english-books-1641-1700_patrologiae-cursus-completus-_1866_160_djvu.txt (OCR text layer of the archive.org scan of Migne PG vol. 160, 1866; item page https://archive.org/details/bim_early-english-books-1641-1700_patrologiae-cursus-completus-_1866_160)
licence: Migne PG (1857-1866) is public domain. The archive.org record gives no licence field (UNVERIFIED for the scan itself).
authenticity_note: Genuine per the Migne index (Confessio fidei posterior, cols. 333-352) and per the Ziaka/Cambridge snippet I saw (not opened). Addressed to Muslim scholars at Mehmed II's request, according to the Migne heading.
notes: The Migne heading says the text was translated into Turkish-Arabic script by a certain Achmoites, a Beroea judge, and printed by Brassicanus in Vienna 1530 (per index/notes read; the 1530 date is from a search snippet). The text names no prophet and does not name Muhammad in the Latin I read.

title_orig: Σύντομος καὶ σαφὴς περὶ τινων κεφαλαίων τῆς ἡμετέρας πίστεως, ἐπὶ τῆς διαλέξεως γεγονὼς μετὰ φίλου τοῦ Μαχουμέτου (Sermocinatio brevis et sapiens de nonnullis capitibus fidei nostrae, de quibus disputavit cum amico Machumetis)
title_es: Diálogo breve y sabio sobre algunos capítulos de nuestra fe, debatido con un amigo de Mahoma (Confessio fidei I, atribuida en el índice de Migne)
title_en: Brief and wise dialogue on some articles of our faith, held with a friend of Machumetes (Confessio fidei I)
language: Greek, with Latin printed beside it in Migne
licence: Migne PG public domain; archive.org record gives no licence field (UNVERIFIED)
authenticity_note: DISPUTED. The Migne index attributes it to Gennadios as 'Confessio fidei I'. A search snippet of the Ziaka/Cambridge article says cols. 319A-332C are a different, pseudo-Athanasian work. I did not open the article; treat as UNVERIFIED.
notes: Only the title names 'Machumetis'; the body is a Trinitarian and Christological dialogue with a Turkish interlocutor and does not name Muhammad in the text I read.

title_orig: Ducae, Michaelis Ducae nepotis, Historia byzantina
title_es: Historia bizantina (Historia Turco-Byzantina) de Miguel Ducas
title_en: Historia Byzantina of Michael Doukas (Historia Turco-Byzantina)
language: Greek, with Latin printed beside it (Bekker 1834)
edition_original: Bekker, Corpus Scriptorum Historiae Byzantinae (Bonn: Weber, 1834); Greek text with Latin version (Boulliau 1649 revised by Bekker, per the archive.org record). Page numbers in my citations are the Bekker pagination printed in the scan.
edition_english: Magoulias 1975 translation (in copyright; NOT used). No public-domain English found.
digital_url: https://archive.org/download/bub_gb_fNQFAAAAQAAJ/bub_gb_fNQFAAAAQAAJ_djvu.txt (OCR); scan page images read at https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_fNQFAAAAQAAJ (PDF pages 39, 134, 254 checked visually)
licence: archive.org metadata: Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0
authenticity_note: Genuine (Doukas). Some Latin sections in the Bekker volume are a 15th-century Italian translation printed afterwards and are not Doukas' Greek; I did not use them.
notes: Doukas writes 'Mahometes' in the Latin for the Sultan Mehmed (Mehmed I/II), NOT for the Prophet; passages must be read in context. The Greek 'Μωαμέδ' refers to the Prophet.

title_orig: Γεωργίου Φραντζῆ Χρονικὸν μεῖζον (Chronicon maius), Libri I-IV
title_es: Crónica mayor (Chronicon maius) atribuida a Jorge Sfrantzes
title_en: Chronicon maius attributed to George Sphrantzes
date: authorship disputed; text likely 16th century (see authenticity_note)
language: Greek, with Latin printed beside it (Bekker 1838)
edition_original: Bekker, Corpus Scriptorum Historiae Byzantinae 33 (Bonn: Weber, 1838), with Ioannes Cananus and Ioannes Anagnostes. Migne PG 156 is the other printing (not read).
edition_english: Philippides 1980 translation (in copyright; NOT used). No public-domain English found.
licence: archive.org record gives no licence field; the 1733 Latin Pasquali printing on archive.org is marked CC Public Domain Mark (UNVERIFIED for the 1838 scan)
authenticity_note: DISPUTED. The Maius is generally regarded as a later compilation, not Sphrantzes' own text: a Cambridge guide snippet attributes it to a 16th-century author (reported as Makarios Melissenos; not opened). The Minus is the text usually attributed to Sphrantzes. Book IV contains a Latin-and-Greek polemic against Muhammad presented as a separate section.
notes: Only OCR text of the scan was used; Greek OCR errors are present (noted in passages). The Chronicon minus was NOT found in this Bekker volume (negative result).
